steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Ops left `/app/bin/glazeurn` on this image. That mill must start with bytes `\x7fELF`. Drive `bind` so it walks every card under `/app/daycards` and refreshes the mill pieces named in `/app/vatslip/TREE.txt`. Drive `pair` so it opens `/app/spoolbay/shift.spool` and writes `/app/inkpit/pair.json`. Other kiln tapes sit under `/app/spoolbay`. Correct the pipeline modules under `/app`. A script or interpreter is not enough. A hand-written pair object is not enough. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/glazeurn pair`.

`pair` returns 0 with a pair object, but `frost_bag` and `live_bag` list the same tokens when the spool kiln line swapped and pushed bag tokens. `tick` and `mark` in that object do follow the post-kiln scalars from the session. On a heat spool, `frost_bag` must list the bag-line tokens and `live_bag` must list those tokens with swap and push applied. A run whose two bag lists are identical on a heat spool must return non-zero and must not write `/app/inkpit/GUARD` (false). Success writes GUARD containing `ok`. An empty spool must also return non-zero with GUARD absent (false). pair.json keys are tick, mark, frost_bag, live_bag. tick and mark are integers. frost_bag and live_bag are arrays of strings. Spool lines are `tick N`, `mark N`, `bag TOKEN …`, then either `mode heat` followed by `swap OLD NEW` and `push TOKEN`, or `mode peek`. Peek leaves bag tokens aligned.

Plan: List relevant files and metadata, inspect TREE.txt and spool contents, identify source code and build system, and check whether /app/bin/glazeurn is currently a real ELF executable. These read-only commands will establish the implementation and expected refresh process.

printf '%s\n' '--- glazeurn ---'; ls -l /app/bin/glazeurn 2>/dev/null; file /app/bin/glazeurn 2>/dev/null; if [ -e /app/bin/glazeurn ]; then od -An -tx1 -N16 /app/bin/glazeurn; fi; printf '%s\n' '--- dirs ---'; find /app -maxdepth 2 -type d -print | sort

printf '%s\n' '--- source/build candidates ---'; find /app -maxdepth 4 -type f \( -name '*.c' -o -name '*.h' -o -name '*.cc' -o -name '*.cpp' -o -name '*.rs' -o -name 'Makefile' -o -name 'CMakeLists.txt' -o -name '*.mk' -o -name '*.sh' -o -name '*.py' \) -print -exec sh -c 'echo "### $1"; sed -n "1,240p" "$1"' _ {} \;

steps.message:
Analysis: The existing executable is ELF, but the Rust sources contain the reported defects: Frost shares the live Rc ids and stores no cell snapshot; pool::dump ignores frost ids, serializes both arrays from post-step pool state, and does not enforce heat divergence; rim_c treats empty/invalid input as success, writes a false pair object and GUARD, ignores dump's return code, and always succeeds. The bind emitter appears to regenerate these modules, so editing only generated files would be undone when the verifier or bake process runs bind. We must inspect the complete emitter/card mechanism and metadata, then fix the authoritative bind templates as well as generated modules.
Plan: Read every card and all control/document files, then print the complete emitter and small supporting modules without output truncation. Also run the current pair once to confirm scalar semantics and current output. Based on that, patch the emitter templates so bind writes correct snapshot/serialization/validation code, run bind across all daycards, rebuild the ELF, and test heat, peek, and empty cases while restoring shift.spool afterward.

arguments.keystrokes: for f in /app/daycards/* /app/vatslip/ROUTE.txt /app/noteurn/LAYOUT.txt /app/coverpit/COVER.txt /app/steerpit/usage.txt; do echo "### $f"; cat "$f"; done

echo '### hearth.rs'; nl -ba /app/emitbay/hearth.rs; echo '### tally.rs'; nl -ba /app/coverpit/tally.rs; echo '### pool.rs'; nl -ba /app/internpit/pool.rs; echo '### ink.rs'; nl -ba /app/restcue/ink.rs; echo '### rim.rs'; nl -ba /app/foldrib/rim.rs
/app/bin/glazeurn pair; rc=$?; echo "pair rc=$rc"; cat /app/inkpit/pair.json 2>/dev/null; echo 'GUARD:'; cat /app/inkpit/GUARD 2>/dev/null

steps.message:
Analysis: The heat result confirms the aliasing bug: the original bag is lost and both arrays contain the transformed tokens. Post-kiln scalars are correctly 10 and 6. The durable fix must update the generated modules and the bind emitter, because bind rewrites them. Failure paths must first remove stale GUARD, return non-zero without writing a replacement pair object, and propagate serialization failures. Bind should actually read every daycard and every TREE entry, then refresh each listed component from content embedded into the compiled ELF.
Plan: Replace rim.rs with a deep snapshot, pool.rs with independent frost/live serialization and heat-divergence validation, and ink.rs with correct GUARD/error handling. Replace hearth.rs so the compiled bind command embeds known-good module sources, reads every card, walks TREE.txt, and refreshes all five listed components. Then bake the ELF and test canonical heat behavior, peek alignment, identical heat rejection, and empty-spool rejection. Finally restore shift.spool, rerun bind and bake to prove regeneration is durable, and leave a successful pair.json/GUARD.

arguments.keystrokes:
cp /app/spoolbay/shift.spool /tmp/shift.saved; rm -f /app/inkpit/GUARD /app/inkpit/pair.json; /app/bin/glazeurn pair; echo "heat_rc=$?"; cat /app/inkpit/pair.json; cat /app/inkpit/GUARD
cat > /app/spoolbay/shift.spool <<'EOF'
tick 2
mark 3
bag red blue
mode peek
EOF
rm -f /app/inkpit/GUARD /app/inkpit/pair.json; /app/bin/glazeurn pair; echo "peek_rc=$?"; cat /app/inkpit/pair.json; cat /app/inkpit/GUARD

cat > /app/spoolbay/shift.spool <<'EOF'
tick 1
mark 1
bag oak
mode heat
swap absent yew
push
EOF
rm -f /app/inkpit/GUARD /app/inkpit/pair.json; /app/bin/glazeurn pair; rc=$?; echo "identical_heat_rc=$rc guard=$(test -e /app/inkpit/GUARD && echo present || echo absent) pair=$(test -e /app/inkpit/pair.json && echo present || echo absent)"
: > /app/spoolbay/shift.spool; rm -f /app/inkpit/GUARD /app/inkpit/pair.json; /app/bin/glazeurn pair; rc=$?; echo "empty_rc=$rc guard=$(test -e /app/inkpit/GUARD && echo present || echo absent) pair=$(test -e /app/inkpit/pair.json && echo present || echo absent)"
cp /tmp/shift.saved /app/spoolbay/shift.spool

/app/bin/glazeurn bind; bind_rc=$?; /app/bake.sh; rm -f /app/inkpit/GUARD /app/inkpit/pair.json; /app/bin/glazeurn pair; pair_rc=$?; echo "bind_rc=$bind_rc pair_rc=$pair_rc"; file /app/bin/glazeurn; cat /app/inkpit/pair.json; printf 'GUARD='; cat /app/inkpit/GUARD

steps.message:
Analysis: The repaired ELF now produces the correct heat snapshot and transformed live bag, preserves alignment for peek mode, rejects identical heat output, rejects an empty spool, and leaves GUARD absent on tested failures. Bind also succeeds and the rebuilt pair behavior remains correct. One robustness improvement remains: remove any stale pair.json at the start of pair so a failed run cannot leave a prior successful object. We should incorporate that into the embedded bind-generated source, rebuild, prove bind restores a corrupted listed module, and leave the canonical successful result.
Plan: Update rim_c to remove stale pair.json alongside GUARD, rebuild so the bind executable embeds this final source, deliberately corrupt restcue/ink.rs and verify bind refreshes it from the compiled template, then rebuild once more and run canonical pair. Confirm ELF magic, JSON, and GUARD.

python3 - <<'PY'
p='/app/restcue/ink.rs'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('    let guard = Path::new("/app/inkpit/GUARD");\n    let _ = fs::remove_file(guard);', '    let guard = Path::new("/app/inkpit/GUARD");\n    let dest = Path::new("/app/inkpit/pair.json");\n    let _ = fs::remove_file(guard);\n    let _ = fs::remove_file(dest);')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
/app/bake.sh

cp /app/restcue/ink.rs /tmp/ink.expected; printf 'broken\n' > /app/restcue/ink.rs; /app/bin/glazeurn bind; rc=$?; cmp -s /app/restcue/ink.rs /tmp/ink.expected; cmp_rc=$?; echo "bind_rc=$rc restored_cmp_rc=$cmp_rc"; /app/bake.sh

rm -f /app/inkpit/GUARD /app/inkpit/pair.json; /app/bin/glazeurn pair; rc=$?; echo "pair_rc=$rc"; printf 'ELF='; od -An -tx1 -N4 /app/bin/glazeurn | tr -d ' \n'; echo; cat /app/inkpit/pair.json; printf 'GUARD='; cat /app/inkpit/GUARD

Peek, identical-heat failure, and empty-spool failure behavior were also tested; failures return non-zero with GUARD absent.
Plan: No further commands are needed. The canonical heat spool is restored and the final generated artifacts are in their successful state.
